documents.title: Eye Examination Report
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
EYE EXAMINATION
Date of exam: 01/13/2026
Reason: baseline screening before long-term hydroxychloroquine (started 12/2025 by rheumatology).

Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS with correction. Pupils equal, no afferent defect. Intraocular pressures normal. Anterior segments quiet. Dilated fundus exam: healthy optic nerves, maculae flat with normal foveal reflex, vessels and periphery normal OU.
Automated 10-2 visual fields: full OU, reliable.
SD-OCT macula: normal retinal layers OU, no parafoveal thinning.

Impression: normal baseline exam, no evidence of hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity.
Plan: annual screening beginning after 5 years of use, sooner if visual symptoms.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Albuterol refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, could I get a refill on my albuterol? I left one at my mom's and the other is about empty. Still only using it a couple of times a week.

documents.title: RE: Albuterol refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Megan, the doctor approved it and it went to your pharmacy this morning, two inhalers so you can keep a spare. If you find you're using it more than usual, let us know.

documents.title: Home Infusion Pharmacy
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home-infusion pharmacy called: insurer's annual reauthorization for weekly alpha-1 augmentation is being handled by pulmonology, they only needed the current med list and allergy status for their file. Confirmed NKDA and current meds, including hydroxychloroquine added by rheumatology in December. No action needed from PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

S: 39F here for her yearly.
- RA: on hydroxychloroquine 200 BID since December. Saw rheumatology in March: morning stiffness now about 15 minutes instead of most of the morning, hands and knees hurt less, staying on the same dose. She did not get a note from that visit and neither did we. Uses ibuprofen maybe once a week now.
- Raynaud: fewer attacks with gloves and layering, a few over the winter.
- Alpha-1 with emphysema: weekly home infusions continue without problems. Breathing steady, walks most days, morning cough lighter.
- Asthma: fluticasone BID, albuterol a couple of times a week.
- Eczema: quiet, cream now and then.
- Baseline eye exam in January normal.

Meds: fluticasone HFA 110 2 puffs BID; albuterol HFA prn; triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID (rheum); alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg IV weekly (pulm); ibuprofen 200 mg OTC prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol. Still designing, mostly from home.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: well.
Lungs: diminished at the bases with prolonged expiration, no wheeze, unchanged.
Heart regular, no murmur.
Abd soft, no organomegaly.
Hands: fingers pink and warm, no ulcers.
Skin: clear today.
Ext: no edema.

A/P
1. RA: improving on hydroxychloroquine per rheumatology. CBC with diff and CMP today.
2. Raynaud: conservative measures working.
3. AATD/emphysema: stable on augmentation, followed by pulmonology. Yearly liver tests today.
4. Asthma, eczema: no changes.
5. Health maintenance: turns 40 in January, so we talked about starting screening mammograms then; she'd like to. Pap/HPV due 2027. Flu and COVID vaccines at the October visit.

RTC October.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Megan, your blood counts, kidney function and liver tests from Tuesday are all normal, which is what we want to see on hydroxychloroquine and with alpha-1. Enjoy the summer and see you in October.

documents.title: Fluticasone refill and October appt
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, the pharmacy says my fluticasone is out of refills. Also just checking I'm still on for October 13 in the morning, I have it in my calendar.

documents.title: RE: Fluticasone refill and October appt
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Megan, you're confirmed for Tuesday 10/13 at 9:20. The refill request went to the doctor and was approved this morning, a 90-day supply with refills is at your pharmacy.
